properties.name: Seven Labors of Rostam
properties.summary: The greatest hero of Persian legend, Rostam, completed seven impossible tasks to rescue King Kavus: slaying a lion, surviving the desert, defeating a dragon, overcoming a sorceress, capturing a demon, surviving a storm, and slaying the White Demon. His tragic fate was killing his own son Sohrab in battle.

properties.name: Ahura Mazda vs Angra Mainyu
properties.summary: Ahura Mazda (Wise Lord) created the world from pure thought. His adversary Angra Mainyu (Destructive Spirit) corrupted creation with disease, death, and evil. History is the 12,000-year cosmic battle between truth (asha) and falsehood (druj). At the end, a Saoshyant (savior) will purify the world in molten metal, defeating evil forever.

properties.name: Zal and the Simorgh
properties.summary: Zal, born with white hair, was abandoned on Mount Damavand by his ashamed father Sam. The Simorgh, a benevolent mythical bird, raised him. When Sam repented, the Simorgh returned Zal with one of her feathers — when burned, she would come to his aid. Zal married Rudabeh and fathered the hero Rostam.

properties.name: Yima's Vara — Persian Flood Myth
properties.summary: Ahura Mazda warned King Yima of a coming winter that would destroy all life. He instructed Yima to build a vara (enclosure) and fill it with the finest specimens of every living thing — seeds, animals, and humans. After the great winter passed, Yima's vara repopulated the world.

properties.name: Kay Kavus Flies to Heaven
properties.summary: The vainglorious king Kay Kavus attempted to fly to heaven by harnessing eagles to his throne with meat tied above them on lances. The eagles flew upward seeking the meat. When exhausted, the eagles and throne crashed into a forest. Rostam had to rescue the humiliated king, as always.
